The current CAS persistence formats comprise protobuf metadata with CasHeader, a fixed binary CABL envelope, CARN block-framed records, a binary CAPT part manifest, strict tagged text controls, raw passthrough files, and the exceptional unversioned GcHeartbeat.
Blob objects are stored at <prefix>/blobs/<first-two-hex-chars>/<32-hex-blob-id>, produced by Layout::blobKey
A CABL blob has a fixed-size CasEnvelope header followed by raw payload bytes, with blob_header_len normally 256 and an envelope core of 94 bytes
A blob's incarnation zone is excluded from logical_hash, so a new physical incarnation can have a different token without changing the blob id
decodeEnvelopeHeader validates CABL magic, compatibility_version, critical extensions, header length, object-size arithmetic, and header_hash
cas_pool_meta stores pool_id, blob_header_len, gc_shards, min_reader_generation, and algos_used at <prefix>/_pool_meta
The persisted gc_shards value in cas_pool_meta is authoritative; a node reopening with a different local PoolConfig::gc_shards must use the persisted value
A CARS RootShardManifest is the single commit point for namespace refs, mapping user-visible refs to immutable part manifests and carrying the ordered journal used for reachability deltas
RootShardManifest ref maps are name-sorted by std::map, while journal order is insertion order and should follow transition_version order
ManifestRef alone is not globally unique; the protocol identity is ManifestId = (RootNamespace, ManifestRef)
A CAPT PartManifest contains a 4-byte CAPT magic, a 16-bit format_version, writer_version, ManifestRef, root_namespace_id, payload_digest, and an embedded CARN stream of ManifestEntries
Store::readManifest checks that the journal ManifestRef matches the decoded part-manifest body and that the decoded namespace matches the owning namespace
PartManifest.payload_digest is persisted but is not generally validated by Store::readManifest, so it is not currently a complete integrity guarantee

The embedded CARN stream in PartManifest should be retained only if PartManifest gains a real streaming reader or shares typed CARN validation; otherwise CAPT should become fully self-contained custom binary or protobuf
A CARN record stream has a 13-byte header, CRC-protected sorted blocks, and a CRC-protected sparse footer index that supports RunFileReader::seek
Typed CARN open helpers should validate the expected RunKind, key_schema, codec, and block-size invariants before callers interpret records

RunFile is justified for large sorted streams requiring bounded-memory merge, ranged seek, and replay or adoption of write-once run objects, but is less compelling for small embedded sections materialized whole
GcStateProto.retired_refs is semantically load-bearing for the ack-floor writer gate; an old reader cannot safely ignore it without a compatibility gate or documented mixed-version rule
GcHeartbeat is exactly 24 bytes: a 16-byte big-endian GC owner id followed by an 8-byte big-endian heartbeat sequence, with no magic or version field
The unversioned GcHeartbeat is acceptable only as disposable advisory state; if it affects cross-version safety it must be converted to protobuf with CasHeader
A cas_fold_seal contains rfl ref-life rows, sorted btr blob-target RunRef rows, and shard-sorted cnd condemned summaries, followed by a record-count trailer
cas_fold_seal is a write-once deterministic artifact produced by encodeFoldSeal and putDeterministicArtifact, so replay of the same attempt must reproduce identical bytes

Fold-seal catalog admission reserves the full worst-case shape using saturating arithmetic: the widest fixed frame, one widest rfl row per catalog entry, and one widest btr plus cnd row for each persisted gc_shards value
Each RunRef btr row carries the whole-object chained CityHash128 checksum, and GC verifies that checksum before acting on the referenced run
gc_shards > 1 uses target-sharded data layout and a local reducer loop inside one Gc::fold call; production does not schedule reducer shards across replicas or workers
The historical part_manifest_cleanup CARN run design is removed: current post-CAS manifest deletion uses the in-memory folded.mf_cleanup map and orphan sweep scans cas/manifests/ directly
RetiredSetProto records exact incarnation tokens, and GC deletes only the observed incarnation so a replacement object is not deleted accidentally
GcOutcomeLogProto makes destructive GC decisions idempotent and auditable by recording delete and recheck outcomes for replay and observability
OwnerProto at <prefix>/gc/server-roots/<srid>/owner is a sticky binding from server_root_id to server UUID and prevents silent reuse under a different UUID
ServerEpochProto provides durable monotone writer-epoch allocation so a fenced writer cannot reuse the same epoch after reopen
MountLeaseProto is live lease and ack-floor state, not identity; server identity belongs to OwnerProto

Namespace verbatim files at <prefix>/roots/<ns>/_files/<relative-path> and mountpoint objects at <prefix>/roots/<relative-path> are raw passthrough bytes whose integrity belongs to their external file formats
Persisted token values remain opaque strings and token_type, rather than provider-specific string shape, determines whether a token is ETag, generation, or emulated
The intended versioning convention is writer_version for forensic producer generation, compatibility_version as the read gate, and format_version only for a local codec layout version
PartManifest and RunFile fields named format_version currently act as compatibility_version because they are passed to checkCompatibility
Every persisted CAS object should document its storage key and owner, body family, magic or no-magic reason, producer and consumers, determinism, versioning, integrity, decoder invariants, and tests
cas_format.proto should remain the single normative protobuf file, with its magic table completed for OwnerProto, ServerEpochProto, and MountLeaseProto

RunFile and PartManifest should rename format_version to compatibility_version at the next incompatible break or add a separate local format_version while reserving compatibility_version for G_BUILD gating
RunFile block and footer CRC32C should remain until RunRef.checksum is either verified as a full-run artifact hash before trust or removed or demoted before release
Typed CARN helpers should include openManifestEntriesRun, openBlobTargetRun, and openPartManifestCleanupRun and validate RunKind, key_schema, codec, and block-size invariants
If GcHeartbeat remains fixed binary, it must be documented as disposable advisory state with exact-length validation and permission for future readers to ignore or recreate it

Decoder errors should classify bad magic, truncation, duplicate keys, wrong owner, invalid enum, and invalid length as CORRUPTED_DATA, while future compatibility_version or unknown critical extensions are UNKNOWN_FORMAT_VERSION
Unused FormatId::Roster, unused RunKind values, TreeId without a live type boundary, and distributed sharded-GC scaffolding should be removed or demoted unless current producers and consumers exist

The recommended codec cleanup order is comments and magic tables, enum and hash validation, RunFile record-bound checks, RunRef.checksum and payload_digest decisions, GcHeartbeat decision, binary version naming, and unused-placeholder removal
CAS codec proposal v2 assumes pre-release data with no dual-read compatibility scaffolding and one atomic cutover per format
Every self-describing CAS object in v2 begins with one universal 8-byte little-endian CasPreamble containing magic, writer_version, and compatibility_version
The v2 CasPreamble layout is [0,4) magic, [4,6) writer_version u16, and [6,8) compatibility_version u16
v2 gates compatibility_version on the raw preamble before parsing any body bytes, so a future object reports UNKNOWN_FORMAT_VERSION rather than a parse error
The v2 Proto family uses a 32-byte CasProtoFrame with body_codec, flags, reserved, body_crc32c, body_len, and raw_len after the 8-byte preamble
v2 Proto decoding validates frame fields, exact remaining body_len, and raw_len <= cap(FormatId) before allocating, verifies body_crc32c, decompresses if needed, and only then parses protobuf
The shared v2 helpers encodeFramedProto and decodeFramedProto own framing, compression, magic, compatibility, and parse boilerplate; per-object codecs only map fields and validate invariants
The v2 Stream family uses a 16-byte CasStreamHeader with the universal preamble, kind, key_schema, block_codec, flags, and block_size
v2 callers may open record streams only through typed helpers that validate kind, key_schema, block_codec, and block-size bounds before interpreting records
The v2 stream cursor returns string_view key and payload values valid until the next next or seek call, while one block buffer is reused across block loads
The v2 Payload family keeps CABL constant-offset ranged reads and replaces header_hash with header_crc32c in the guard slot while leaving payload bytes unchanged
In v2 writer_version is forensic only, compatibility_version is the only read gate, and format_version is deleted rather than retained as a third version field
v2 additive protobuf fields that are safe to ignore need no version bump, while breaking or reinterpreted fields require a compatibility_version bump via currentCompatibilityVersion
v2 Proto bodies use one whole-body zstd frame when raw_len is at least the default 4 KiB threshold, while readers accept compressed and uncompressed bodies unconditionally
v2 deterministic formats written through putDeterministicArtifact must use body_codec = 0 because adoption compares bytes and compressed bytes depend on the vendored zstd version
v2 rejects ClickHouse CompressedWriteBuffer for CAS bodies and chooses plain single-frame zstd so the protocol remains portable outside ClickHouse
v2 integrity requires every byte range interpreted by CAS to have exactly one fail-closed guard verified before trust at the granularity of the read unit
In v2 CRC32C is the corruption guard and CityHash128 is the identity or equality proof; the two primitives have disjoint roles
v2 changes CasEnvelope.header_hash to header_crc32c at [86,90), with [90,94) as a zero u32, while keeping the 94-byte core
RunRefProto.checksum in v2 is CityHash128 over the full stored run object and is used for adoption and fsck identity, not as a read-path guard
v2 drops PartManifest.payload_digest because body_crc32c subsumes its guard role and the field was neither a key nor verified during reads
v2 caps Proto decode raw_len at 1 MiB for singletons, 64 MiB for CARS root shards, and 256 MiB for CAPT, retired sets, outcome logs, and fold seals
v2 stream objects have no body cap because resident memory is one block with a hard cap of 1 MiB plus a bounded footer index

The v2 format registry requires one FormatId entry with magic, family, cap, and compression policy, one codec pair, one storage key, one golden and corruption test, and one codecs.md row per persisted object
The v2 shared test harness covers round trips, golden bytes, frame truncation, CRC corruption, future compatibility, wrong magic, nonzero flags or reserved fields, and cap-before-allocation
v2 Proto decoding performs exactly one raw_len-sized body allocation, while the Stream reader allocates one reusable hard-cap block buffer and next returns views into it
v2 rejects an all-protobuf design because unbounded GC data would lose bounded-memory streaming and ranged seek
v2 rejects FlatBuffers and Cap'n Proto because CAS metadata is small and object-storage network latency dominates parsing, while the dependencies add no needed portability
v2 migration order is shared framing, reframe Proto objects, move CAPT to Proto, update Streams, frame heartbeat and swap envelope guard, enable compression, then update docs and tooling
The v2 target reduces the format structure from five families plus one exception to three families plus explicit raw passthrough and reduces version gates to one name pair at one pre-parse position
CAS codec proposal v3 supersedes codecs_proposal_v2.md in full and treats the pre-release system as requiring one cutover per format with no dual-read compatibility scaffolding
v3 makes every metadata byte human-readable with head, zstdcat, jq, less, and diff; raw blob payload remains the only non-metadata binary region
Every v3 CAS object uses a header line, a body, and an optional trailer line; type identifies the object and v is the only compatibility version
v3 gates v > G_BUILD from line 1 before touching the body and reports UNKNOWN_FORMAT_VERSION; unknown !-prefixed keys also fail closed with UNKNOWN_FORMAT_VERSION
v3 compression is whole-object single-frame zstd selected per type: Always types use a .zst key suffix and all other types are raw without a suffix
v3 has no writer_version or format_version; forensic provenance is carried by ch and bld where needed, while currentCompatibilityVersion and changePoints remain stamping machinery
Unknown noncritical keys are skipped on tolerant objects and rejected as CORRUPTED_DATA on strict deterministic objects; duplicate keys are always CORRUPTED_DATA
Every v3 padding zone, including envelope header padding and manifest inter-file gaps, has deterministic expected content regenerated and verified by the decoder
v3 separates Control JSON objects, sorted NDJSON record streams, and Payload hybrid objects; namespace verbatim files and mountpoint objects remain raw non-family passthroughs

Tiny control types cas_pool_meta, cas_gc_state, cas_gc_hb, cas_owner, cas_epoch, cas_mount_lease, and cas_blob_meta are raw bare JSON, while cas_ref_snap, cas_ref_log, and cas_gc_outcomes are Always-compressed .zst controls
v3 cas_run uses sorted NDJSON records with marker words edge, zero, and condemned, followed by a trailer count n
Every cas_run consumer reads the whole file sequentially, accumulates RunRef.checksum over the read, verifies it before acting, and uses trailer n to detect line-boundary truncation
The v3 hex NDJSON encoding is estimated at about twice the bytes of the retired binary encoding, roughly 1 GB versus 500 MB for 10M records
v3 cas_part_manifest stores JSON descriptor lines followed by a raw payload zone with head -v-style banners; inline offsets exclude banners and padding
v3 rejects base64 for inline manifest bytes because it blinds mostly-text sidecars and moves payload into the descriptor; inline payload remains a separate raw zone
Part-manifest trailer fields n and plen guard descriptor truncation and descriptor-to-zone length consistency; v3 intentionally has no payload hash
The v3 cas_blob header occupies exactly 256 bytes: JSON occupies [0,json_len), spaces occupy [json_len,255), and byte 255 is a newline
The v3 cas_blob tag is a fresh random u128 per upload attempt and is the exact-token delete primitive; bld attributes newborn debris to the writer build
The v3 cas_blob envelope retains constant payload offset blob_header_len = 256 and does not use frame-level compression because payload identity is the raw bytes
v3 drops cas_blob hash_algo, domain_id, header_hash, writer_version, logical_size, and logical_hash because they are redundant, unvalidated, replaced by ch and bld, or already absent from code
v3 deterministic objects are exactly the fold seal and GC runs; they are raw, strict-key, fixed-order, sorted-iteration artifacts passed through putDeterministicArtifact
v3 uses CityHash128 for identity, zstd XXH64 for compressed-body corruption guards, and delegates uncompressed local-file and blob-payload integrity to provider, MergeTree, or fsck layers
The per-object evolution gates are v <= G_BUILD, a pool min_reader_generation forward floor and backward format floor at mount, and a future roster-based fleet floor designed but not yet built
On mutable objects, additive JSON fields are designed to be safe-to-lose because an old-build read-modify-write can omit them until the pool floor rises
Breaking v3 changes use a version-keyed encoder ladder that writes the field set valid at the pool floor, and the floor raise fences old binaries at mount
For deterministic formats, a re-deriving writer must re-encode at the v read from the existing adopted object's header line so leader failover across an upgrade remains byte-matching
v3 line caps are 64 KiB for singleton and ref objects, 64 KiB descriptor lines for cas_part_manifest, 4 KiB for cas_run records, and exactly 256 bytes for the cas_blob header
Provider metadata is only a mirror for eyes and dashboards; the CAS protocol never reads it and must fail closed if it is absent
v3 places all codecs in Core/Formats and forbids Formats from including CasBackend or CasStore; a codec needing a backend does not compile
The v3 format checklist requires one FormatId entry, one mapping-only codec in Formats, one documented CasLayout key, one shared-harness registration, and one Formats/README.md row
The v3 shared test harness covers readable golden text, line truncation, v+1, wrong type, unknown keys, duplicate keys, cap-before-allocation, and padding or banner mutation

v3 deletes cas_format.proto and protobuf build dependencies, CARN blocks and footer seek machinery, the binary envelope codec and TLV parser, refsnaplog binary codecs, the heartbeat fixed-record codec, the part-manifest cleanup run, and most of CasInspect
v3 rejects v2's framed protobuf design because it keeps the control plane behind bespoke tooling and adds integrity guards whose failures change no decision
v3 rejects Avro and Parquet for cas_run because seek is dead in production, they add dependencies, and their container or row-group machinery does not fit two-hash marker records
v3 rejects keeping per-block CRC and footer in cas_run because the seal checksum covers the whole file that all consumers actually read
The v3 migration order is Formats bootstrap, control plane, refsnaplog, blob meta, runs, part manifest, blob envelope, and final provider-metadata and build-wiring cleanup
v3 targets three families plus explicit raw passthrough, zero unversioned objects, one version field gated on line 1, and removal of protobuf and code generation from the subsystem
Recovery can publish seal S without advancing result.state.greatest_applied to S, so the next epoch's first log uses prev=A instead of prev=S and GC can accept a late void log below the cursor
The orphan-manifest sweep can delete a committed manifest when a hot LIST omits the logs that grant its owner, because activeManifestKeys trusts only the incomplete reconstructed set
Using {0,0} as a rebirth anchor after retiring a namespace cursor destroys durable lineage: an old log can be folded twice, while preserving prev=R can leave a missing retired anchor
An empty unclean recovery publishes no seal, so a genuinely void first record has no durable certificate and can be folded as writer-unapplied data or skipped without proof
Snapshot cleanup can delete a recovery-seal chain anchor before durable_cursor reaches it because ordinary snapshot deletion is not gated by the cursor
B1 and B2 are undefined for repaired and certified-void records when logs_applied counts only fully folded listed logs and repair paths bypass TxnApplyLedger::open

A chain-repair 404 can be legitimate after concurrent snapshot publication and deletion, so recovery must route it through a bounded vanish-restart loop rather than classify it immediately as corruption
Fsck can report clean after an incomplete hot frontier because it silently skips absent snapshot logs and disappearing covered logs and cannot detect a whole omitted namespace
A namespace whose physical deletion remains Pending indefinitely causes every fold seal to carry and rescan an unbounded cleanup set
Recovery repair buffering can exhaust memory because the plan collects an entire omitted run even though transactions can be 20 MiB and current recovery retains only one decoded transaction
RefTxnId allocation can wrap ref_sequence at UINT64_MAX, making a real log id indistinguishable from a seal anchor; the protocol also needs prev < txn_id, cycle detection, and a resource bound
Voidness cannot be inferred from recovery's {my_epoch - 1, UINT64_MAX} seal because burned mount epochs can make the seal's epoch differ from the actual dead writer epoch
A recovery seal can certify a record X only when seal.sealed_from < X.id and X.id <= seal.snapshot_id; absence of an authoritatively discovered covering interval must hold the namespace
No current field binds a manifest owner grant to the ref-transaction cursor because build sequences and ref transaction sequences are independent and MountLease contains no ref cut
Orphan-manifest deletion for live namespaces must be disabled unless a persisted owner-grant ref id or fenced quiescent reconstruction proves the cut

Allowing sealed_from={0,0} does not encode a never-born namespace because Removed without remove_txn_id is rejected by the snapshot codec; an explicit NeverBorn state or separate seal format is required

SYSTEM ... GC REBUILD and fsck remain destructive or cleanliness-sensitive hot-LIST consumers: rebuild can condemn blobs from a wholesale-omitted namespace and fsck cannot know the namespace was omitted
Vanish-restart can discard chain evidence and later succeed from an older snapshot when a second lying LIST omits both the selected successor and its missing predecessor
Embedding every visited namespace in every fold seal is not bounded because fold seals have a 256 MiB control-object limit and namespace churn is unbounded
Pinning every ordinary snapshot above a held cursor can create unbounded snapshot storage, with each snapshot potentially reaching 64 MiB; only recovery-seal ids above the cursor need pinning
B1 accounting must be cut-scoped to records in (parent_cursor, final_cursor]; speculative repaired bodies and void observations above the final cut are separate metrics
A per-namespace hold is pool-wide because an unknown +1 may name any shared blob; global destructive suppression prevents graduation, blob deletion, and ref cleanup for other namespaces too
Repair observability needs the same per-round cap as Probe A, with true totals and truncation status carried in emitted gc_anomaly rows and aggregate counters for omitted rows

A CAS request admitted before fence expiry can remain blocked through claim and grace and complete after recovery lists the namespace because attempt_timeout_ms is only a scheduling check, not a socket deadline
A ghost log V with prev=A can be folded before a later successor reveals recovery seal S, and if the namespace stays quiet no anchor crossing occurs to detect the ghost

An unresolved owner grant can land after its build is retired and min_active advances, so the premise that all grants below R* have settled is false unless R* means inclusive highest allocated or attempted ref id or unresolved builds remain active
A fresh lease with min_active=0 and no prior R* does not safely cover prior-epoch builds; {0,0} is unsafe and a missing bound disables reclamation
A member-wide highest-allocated R* can permanently retain a quiet namespace whose chain ends far below another namespace's allocator high-water
REBUILD cannot prove all member leases are fenced by enumerating them through LIST(gc/server-roots/) while the same hot-LIST trust boundary allows a live member to be omitted
A required recovery floor stored only in an evictable ref-table runtime is lost under cache eviction or self-remount, and recovery can install after remount without a final supersession check
A Pending-cap check is not linearizable when writers append remove_namespace before GC creates Pending entries, and limiting Pending does not bound permanent lineage tombstones
Quarantine metadata must persist first-held round, retry generation, next probe, and offending anchor, and suppress_destructive must remain true for carried quarantine until successful revalidation
A NeverBorn recovery seal needs a specified zero sealed_from exception and seal-aware fsck handling; otherwise a healthy pool whose newest snapshot is synthetic remains unchecked
Quarantine backoff bounds only anchor and repair point reads; every fold still pays for two global ref-prefix enumerations, held-namespace grouping, Probe A comparisons, and larger fold seals
A latest-pointer-only _seal_latest forgets earlier unconsumed void intervals, so a ghost in an earlier interval can be folded after a later seal overwrites the pointer

The proposed min_active acknowledgement does not contain the recovery generation: GC can condemn a ghost, recovery can publish its pointer while down, and later rounds can delete before any pointer-aware fold occurs
An absent _seal_latest cannot prove clean history because deletion, rollback, or loss can make a published authority appear absent; absence must be a hold or corruption condition

The min_active and R* pair has no specified linearization point because min_active and the ref allocator are sampled under separate synchronization, allowing grants after the sampled high-water to be swept
A later first recovery pointer can invalidate a valid clean genesis record with prev=0, and a lineage-only pointer state for removal before any seal is not defined

Seal publication must be an idempotent routine that adopts or publishes the derived immutable seal, reconciles the pointer by semantic read/decode/merge/CAS with exact rereads, and installs only after the pointer contains the adopted descriptor

Quarantine cannot be cleared by an empty or stale listing; revalidation must exact-GET the persisted offender and anchor, reread pointer or generation, and carry quarantine through omission, 404, pointer change, or budget exhaustion

The pointer CAS design is supported by RustFS/AWS and S3-compatible GCS plus EmulatedSingleProcess, but Azure or non-S3 native object storage is not an admitted writable CAS backend under the current single-attempt retry profile
